queries.q: I have an idea for a new PM skill that turns raw NPS verbatims into a themed insight brief - walk me through getting it built into the library.

We keep improvising the same vendor-comparison writeup by hand every quarter, and I bet other teams do too. Is there a real gap in what pm-skills already covers, and if so, help me get something built and staged for review.
queries.notes: Intent-only, problem-first ask with no skill-builder keyword

queries.q: Guide me through creating a new pm-skills skill for writing customer advisory board briefings, from idea to a full packet I can review.
Before I write a single line: our PMs keep hand-rolling the same pricing teardown doc and there's no repo skill that produces it. Is this even worth a new skill?
queries.notes: Intent-only, opens with the gap-analysis question itself

queries.q: Run gap analysis on whether we need a new skill for capacity planning against sprint commitments, and if there's a real gap, take me through the Why Gate and generate the packet.
I want to add a foundation skill for cross-team dependency mapping to the library - help me classify it, pick exemplars, and draft the files.
Take my rough idea - a skill that drafts internal FAQ documents for support handoff - and turn it into a full Skill Implementation Packet with drafts staged for review.
Our team invents a new one-off doc every time we run vendor security reviews. Is that worth turning into a proper skill in the catalog, and if so, build it out end to end.
queries.notes: Intent-only, no artifact keyword until the ask to build it out

queries.q: Help me figure out whether this belongs as a new domain skill or folds into an existing one, then generate the draft SKILL.md, template, example, and eval fixtures for a customer win-loss analysis skill.
I want to propose a new utility skill for auto-generating stakeholder RACI matrices - start with the gap analysis against what's already in the catalog.
The persona skill's example is thin and a couple of checklist items are vague per the last audit - can you tighten up the existing skill rather than start something new?
queries.notes: Improving an already-shipped skill is the iterator's job, not the builder's, per the builder's own When NOT to Use

queries.q: Before we ship this quarter, check whether foundation-okr-writer still meets the repo's structural and quality conventions.
queries.notes: Auditing one existing skill against conventions is the validator's job, not skill creation

queries.q: I want to chain interview-synthesis, opportunity-tree, and prioritization into a durable, reusable workflow the team can invoke as one command.
queries.notes: Multi-skill workflow authoring is a separate builder; the skill-builder explicitly defers workflow creation

queries.q: Run a full pass over the skills catalog and flag drifted headings, stale AGENTS.md entries, and anything that would block the next release.
queries.notes: Repo-wide governance audit across existing skills, not creation of a new one

queries.q: Draft a PRD for the new skill-recommendation feature we're shipping to end users next quarter.
queries.notes: Trap: 'skill' here names an end-user-facing product feature, not a pm-skills library skill; this is a requirements doc ask

queries.q: Help me build a Claude Code skill for my personal recipe-blog repo that turns draft markdown into publish-ready posts.
queries.notes: Non-pm-skills context; the builder's own When NOT to Use points this to a general skill builder instead

queries.q: Help me draft OKRs for the growth pod for H2.
My CI pipeline for the docs site is failing on a Node version mismatch during the build step - can you help debug it?
Find me a good conference room for Thursday's product review and send the invite.
We just shipped a new lead-routing skill for our internal voice assistant - can you write up documentation on how it works for the sales team?
queries.notes: Keyword collision on 'skill' (voice-assistant skill, not a pm-skills library skill); unrelated domain and no packet/gap-analysis intent
